speaker: Doctor
text: I will ask you a few questions to understand your condition better. Can you tell me exactly when your high fever and seizure started, and have you noticed any other symptoms like neck stiffness, rash changes, or confusion?

speaker: Patient
text: 9-month-old infant. The patient is brought in due to a generalized nonpruritic rash for 2 days. The rash started on the trunk and spread to the extremities. Five days ago, the patient had a fever of 40.5°C (104.9°F) and experienced a 1-minute generalized tonic-clonic seizure. The infant was born at term, has no history of serious illness, and her immunizations are up to date. The current medication includes acetaminophen.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Roseola Infantum (Exanthem Subitum).

The history of a high fever followed by a nonpruritic rash appearing after the fever subsides, combined with a seizure likely triggered by the fever spike, is classic for Roseola caused by HHV-6. Given the infant's age and vaccination status, this is the most probable diagnosis. I will confirm the diagnosis by reviewing the rash distribution if you have any photos, but clinically, the presentation is definitive.
